name: UC Davis Department of Viticulture and Enology
summary: University of California wine and grape-growing program where a number of Oregon's founding winemakers trained.

sources.title: UC Davis Department of Viticulture and Enology (Wikipedia)

name: Oregon Wine Board
summary: Semi-independent state agency for Oregon wine marketing and research, established in Oregon statute. It replaced the Oregon Wine Advisory Board, which had operated under the state Department of Agriculture since the early 1980s.

sources.title: Oregon Wine Board Collection: historical note (Linfield University Archives)

name: Oregon Winegrowers Association
summary: Statewide trade association for Oregon growers and wineries, working on legislation, marketing and education. It began in Roseburg in the 1960s and took its current form in 1981 through a merger with the Willamette Valley's Winegrowers Council of Oregon; it petitioned for the Willamette Valley AVA in 1982.

sources.title: Oregon Wine Board Collection: historical note (Linfield University Archives)

name: Willamette Valley Wineries Association
summary: Regional winery association formed in 1983 as the Yamhill County Winegrowers Association by twelve wineries. In 2004 it amended its bylaws to include wineries across the whole Willamette Valley AVA.

name: Oregon State University
summary: Public university in Corvallis whose viticulture and enology research and extension programs, including the Oregon Wine Research Institute, serve the state's wine industry. It is credited with importing Dijon clones of Pinot noir and Chardonnay to the United States and organizing the first International Cool Climate Symposium for Viticulture and Enology in 1984.

sources.title: Oregon's wine industry benefits from OSU research and outreach (OSU Extension Service)

name: Linfield University
summary: University in McMinnville whose campus is the venue of the International Pinot Noir Celebration. The Oregon Wine History Archive was founded there in 2011 to collect and preserve the records and stories of the Oregon wine industry.

sources.title: About the Oregon Wine History Archive

name: Constellation Brands
summary: Publicly traded U.S. drinks company. Its 2022 purchase of Lingua Franca was its first move into Oregon wine.

sources.title: Exclusive: Constellation Buys Oregon's Lingua Franca (Wine Spectator)

name: Ste. Michelle Wine Estates
summary: Wine company that owns Chateau Ste. Michelle in Woodinville, Washington. It bought Erath Winery in 2006.

sources.title: Ste. Michelle buys Oregon winery (NBC News / AP)
Ste. Michelle buys Oregon's Erath Winery (The Spokesman-Review)

name: Groupe Bollinger
summary: Holding company of the Bollinger family, owners of Champagne Bollinger. Ponzi Vineyards, bought in 2021, was its first acquisition outside France.

sources.title: La famille Bollinger acquiert Ponzi Vineyards (SJB / Groupe Bollinger press release, 7 April 2021)
The Bollinger Family to Acquire Ponzi Vineyards (Wine Industry Advisor)

name: Union Wine Company
summary: Oregon wine company owned by Ryan Harms; he and his brother Eric brought Amity Vineyards into the company in 2014.

name: Crimson Wine Group
summary: Napa-based wine holding company whose properties include Pine Ridge, Seghesio, Archery Summit in Oregon and Seven Hills Winery in Walla Walla. In 2016 it also bought the old blocks of Seven Hills Vineyard on the Oregon side of the Walla Walla Valley.

sources.title: Crimson Wine Group Buys 66 Acres of Walla Walla Valley Vines (Wine Spectator)

name: Bacchus Capital Management
summary: San Francisco-based wine private equity firm co-founded in 2007 by Sam Bronfman, Peter Kaufman and Henry Owsley. In 2013 it bought Panther Creek Cellars outright and made a follow-on investment in Wine By Joe.

sources.title: Wine Investment Group Makes Big Moves in Pacific Northwest (Wine Spectator)

name: Santa Margherita USA
summary: U.S. fine wine import subsidiary of Italy's Santa Margherita Gruppo Vinicolo, controlled by the Marzotto family and now trading as HERITA USA. It took majority ownership of ROCO Winery in January 2022.

sources.title: Santa Margherita USA Acquires Majority Ownership of ROCO Winery (Beverage Industry News)
Italian wine group acquires Dundee Hills vineyard from Coppola-owned Domaine Lumineux (Newsberg)

name: Artémis Domaines
summary: François Pinault's wine holding company, owner of Château Latour, Clos de Tart and Eisele Vineyard. In 2022 it took a majority stake in Maisons & Domaines Henriot, the owner of Beaux Frères, with the Henriot family becoming minority shareholders.

sources.title: Château Latour Owner Artémis Domaines Buys Majority Stake in Henriot (Shanken News Daily)

name: Distinguished Vineyards & Wine Partners
summary: Wine company that owns Argyle Winery. Argyle came into the group after Brian Croser's Petaluma winery, which had bought Argyle, was taken over by drinks company Lion Nathan in 2001.

name: Milwaukie Nursery
summary: Orchard and nursery started by Henderson Luelling and William Meek after Luelling's 1847 arrival, at the site where Milwaukie was soon founded. Luelling's brother Seth Lewelling joined in 1850 and took the nursery over when Henderson left for California.

name: LIVE (Low Input Viticulture and Enology)
summary: Sustainability certifier for Pacific Northwest vineyards and wineries, formed by Willamette Valley winegrowers in 1997 and incorporated as a nonprofit in 1999, with accreditation from the international IOBC. It added Washington growers in 2006, a winery program in 2008 and Idaho in 2012.

sources.title: Many winemakers are going easy on the Earth (Sunset)
Wine Person of 2014: Al MacDonald (Oregon Wine Press)

name: Chemeketa Community College
summary: Salem community college whose wine studies program, begun in 1999, is based at the Northwest Wine Studies Center on its Eola campus in West Salem, with an eight-acre teaching vineyard and the Chemeketa Cellars winery.

sources.title: Wine Person of 2014: Al MacDonald (Oregon Wine Press)

name: Deep Roots Coalition
summary: Group of Willamette Valley winemakers and growers that promotes terroir-driven viticulture without irrigation; its members make wine solely from dry-farmed vines.

name: ¡Salud!
summary: Program created in 1991 by Oregon winemakers and Tuality Healthcare professionals to provide basic health care to seasonal vineyard workers, funded mainly by its annual Oregon Pinot Noir Auction. It is now a project of the Hillsboro Medical Center Foundation.

sources.title: ¡Salud! Collection: historical note (Oregon Wine History Archive, Linfield)

name: Erath Family Foundation
summary: Foundation set up by Dick Erath after the 2006 sale of his winery; it has given more than $2 million to wine and viticulture education and research programs at Oregon State University, Linfield and elsewhere.

sources.title: Oregon Wine Pioneer Dick Erath Dies at 87 (Wine Spectator)

name: Southern Oregon University
summary: Public university in Ashland where climatologist Gregory V. Jones was a professor in the Environmental Science and Policy Program and directed the Division of Business, Communication and the Environment.

name: Lycée Viticole de Beaune
summary: Wine-growing school in Beaune, Burgundy, where David Adelsheim spent two months in 1974 studying cool-climate grape varieties and working in its experimental winery.

name: CFPPA de Beaune
summary: School in Beaune, Burgundy, where Luisa Ponzi earned a certificate in viticulture and enology in the early 1990s, the first American woman to complete the course.

sources.title: A Long Story, Still Being Told (Ponzi Vineyards)

name: University of Dijon
summary: Burgundy university where Véronique Drouhin took her advanced degree in enology, and where Raymond Bernard led the clonal selection research that produced the Dijon clones of Pinot noir and Chardonnay.

sources.title: A French woman in Oregon: Véronique Drouhin-Boss (BKWine Magazine)
Clone Wars: Selecting the Right Pinot (SevenFifty Daily)

name: Southern Oregon Research and Extension Center
summary: Oregon State University's experiment station near Medford, built around the pear industry, where wine-grape variety trials planted in the 1960s, in 1990 with Oregon Wine Advisory Board funding, and again in 2017 have guided Rogue Valley growers.

sources.title: Vineyards of the Rogue Valley (Rogue Valley Winegrowers Association)
About us (Oregon Wine Research Institute, OSU)

name: Oregon Wine Research Institute
summary: Research and extension partnership between Oregon State University and the Oregon wine industry, started with about $2 million raised by the industry. OSU sources date its founding to 2008 or 2009.

sources.title: Oregon Wine Research Institute (Oregon's Agricultural Progress, OSU, summer 2014)
James Osborne Named Director of the Oregon Wine Research Institute (OSU College of Agricultural Sciences)
About us (Oregon Wine Research Institute, OSU)

name: Oregon Environmental Council
summary: Portland-based environmental nonprofit that ran the Carbon Neutral Challenge for Oregon wineries with the Oregon Wine Board from 2007 to 2009.

sources.title: 2007-2009: 20% of Oregon's wineries reduced their carbon footprint through our Carbon Neutral Challenge (Oregon Environmental Council)
Oregon eco-winery goes beyond LEED (National Geographic)

name: Oregon Wine Council
summary: Statewide trade association founded in late 2019 by industry members who had opposed labeling legislation sponsored by the Oregon Winegrowers Association; A to Z Wineworks founder Sam Tannahill was an early board member and president.

sources.title: Alternative group forms to promote Oregon wine industry (KATU / Associated Press)

name: Umpqua Valley Winegrowers Association
summary: Roseburg-based association that promotes the wineries and vineyards of the Umpqua Valley.

sources.title: Umpqua Valley Wine History (Umpqua Valley Winegrowers Association)

name: Eola-Amity Hills Winegrowers Association
summary: Association of wineries and growers in the Eola-Amity Hills AVA.

name: Vinovate Custom Wine Services
summary: Custom crush facility in the Dundee Hills that opened in 2023, founded by Rob Townsend, Pam Turner, Scott Baldwin and winemaker Bryan Weil; it makes still and sparkling wines for small brands.

name: Radiant Sparkling Wine Company
summary: Sparkling wine production business started by Andrew Davis that gives other Oregon wineries access to the specialist equipment needed for traditional-method sparkling wine.

name: Southern Oregon Wine Institute
summary: Viticulture and enology program of Umpqua Community College in Roseburg.

name: Hampton Lumber
summary: Family-owned Oregon timber company whose fourth-generation owners moved into wine, planting Tall Tree vineyard in 2016, acquiring Fennwood vineyard in 2018 and buying the Carlton Winemakers Studio in 2021.

name: Vinetenders
summary: Vineyard management company founded by Joel Myers in 1984, which at one point farmed about 500 acres in the northern Willamette Valley.

name: Washington State University
summary: Public university in Pullman, Washington, with a viticulture and enology program; Arabilis founders Kenny and Allison McMahon met there as graduate researchers.

name: AHIVOY
summary: Organization supporting Hispanic vineyard workers in Oregon, co-founded by Jesús Guillén with Sofía Torres McKay and Miguel Lopez and named as he wished.

sources.title: Jesús Guillén Olvera (1980–2018): Réquiem para un gentilhombre (Oregon Wine Press)
